doc.title: Henry Johnson interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995

title: Learning from Joe Williams: knowing the lyrics
summary: Johnson describes accompanying Joe Williams as constant learning, and Williams's lesson that players must know a song's lyrics and story.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Or disappoint if you want to. I want to ask you, tell me about what it’s like to be a guitarist accompanying behind Joe Williams.

It’s a learning situation all the time and it’s an enjoyment because you never know what’s going to happen. Joe has been and done so many things he’s forgotten more stuff that most people know. And I mean you know, you never know when you’re on stage and one of those things are going to come out. He keeps us cracking up all the time. And while you’re cracking up, you have to still be on your toes. So it’s like a real frenetic type of thing going on all the time. But it’s been one of the most enriching experiences of my life, playing with him because he made me see that without the lyrics of the song, you can’t really go out and play a song. Because you don’t know what it’s about. So if you go out and play, you know “Stella By Starlight” just by the notes of the melody, it really

doesn’t mean that much to you. Because you don’t know the little story that’s behind it. So he told me also that most of the guys that were coming up in the 40s and 50s, all the musicians knew the lyrics to the songs. That’s how come they could play a ballad so great. Because they knew the story that’s behind it. And the kids coming up now they don’t learn the lyrics to the songs. They just learn the melody and then they go and play it. But it’s a song that’s not connected with any personal experience they have because they don’t know the story that’s behind it.
You know something else that bothers me is like a lot of the songs that are out today, I don’t know that the lyrics are worth knowing.

There’s very few stories and it seems like people just make a record to see if they can sell, how many pieces of plastic they can sell but it seems to be lacking in authenticity. I want to ask you about something else, because I know that Joe is a master of this. And then I want to see how that affects your guitar playing. And that is you know when a person sings or plays and they are knowledgeable about the effect that their music is having culturally, the music seems to come from a different place inside of them than just because they know the chord or the scale that goes with that.
